reason: All key premises are directly supported by the cited evidence from PMC9572892, which reports the same alloy, boron level, boride precipitation, fracture mode change, and measured property improvements. The evidence is accurately represented with no contradictions or significant gaps.
premises: Boron addition improves grain-boundary cohesion in BCC RHEAs
0.1 at.% B in HfMoNbTaTiZr induces intergranular (Hf,Zr)B2 precipitation
Intergranular borides change fracture mode from intergranular to transgranular
Boron addition increases work hardenability and ductility without major strength loss
Fracture strain increases from ~12% to ~19% with yield strength near or above 1.75 GPa
